_about.what: Beacon Assist Protocol Database (synthetic demo version). One protocol per issue type. Prorio reads it to draft proposed solutions; officers suggest changes; a protocol owner approves; every change bumps the version.
_about.grounding: Steps and timeframes are paraphrased from public Westpac help pages and Australian rules (ePayments Code, AFCA, ASIC RG 271, Moneysmart, ABA), all read on 16 Nov 2026. Each protocol lists its sources. 'team_design' marks a step that is our own design, not a published rule.
_about.not_real: This is not Westpac's internal procedure. It is a demo built from public information.

protocols.title: Customer is being scammed or pressured to move money

protect_first.say: Please don't move any money, and hang up on anyone telling you to. I can lock your accounts and cards right now with SafeBlock. Scheduled payments and money coming in keep working.

steps.step: Tell the customer to stop all contact with the caller and not send more money
Turn on SafeBlock (customer's choice, Face ID step-up)
Draft a payment recall for each linked outgoing transfer and a scam report
Warm handoff; confirm what happened; submit the recall and scam report
Warn the customer about follow-up 'recovery' scams that ask for fees
Send the reference number and next steps in the customer's language

ai_may: ACTIVATE_SAFEBLOCK (only when the customer chooses it)
required_checks: at least one verified account signal for P1 (gate G1)
protocols.customer_message: Your accounts are locked with SafeBlock. A fraud specialist is reviewing case {case_id} now and will try to recover the money. Recovery isn't guaranteed. Never pay anyone who offers to get your money back for a fee.

timeframes.rule: Recall is attempted but not guaranteed

protocols.title: Money taken without the customer's consent

protect_first.say: I can lock your card now so nothing else goes through.

steps.step: Show the merchant details first; unfamiliar names are often a known merchant under a different name
Lock the card or turn on SafeBlock
Stop the card and order a new one; give a case number
Send the transaction investigation request for the customer to confirm and return within 14 days
Investigate and refund if the decision is in the customer's favour

ai_may: BLOCK_CARD (only when the customer chooses it)
required_checks: pending transactions cannot be disputed yet: lock and report
protocols.customer_message: Your card is locked and case {case_id} is open. We'll investigate and tell you the outcome and the reasons.

timeframes.rule: Can take up to 21 working days
Within 21 days: outcome or written notice that more time is needed; investigation done within 45 days unless exceptional
Reports accepted up to 6 years after the customer became aware

protocols.title: Locked out of own money, or suspected account takeover

protect_first.say: If you think someone else got into your account, I can lock it now.

steps.step: Check for recent password, device or contact-detail changes (signal flags from the scoring code)
Verify identity before restoring any access
Restore access or reset sign-in; confirm the Westpac Protect SMS number is the customer's own
Keep the customer updated; offer a callback

ai_may: ACTIVATE_SAFEBLOCK (only when the customer chooses it)
protocols.customer_message: We're checking your account access now (case {case_id}). For your safety, only a person can restore access.

protocols.title: Card lost, stolen or misplaced

protect_first.say: I can lock your card now. If you find it, you can unlock it; it unlocks by itself after 15 days.

steps.step: Ask: misplaced (lock it for up to 15 days) or lost or stolen (cancel and replace)?
Lock the card (temporary) or report it lost or stolen
Check the last transactions for anything the customer doesn't recognise
Approve cancellation and a replacement to the address on file

ai_may: BLOCK_CARD (only when the customer chooses it)
required_checks: confirm the address on file; an address change is a separate officer-only request (gate G3)
protocols.customer_message: Your card is locked. Once approved, a replacement goes to the address we have on file (case {case_id}).

timeframes.rule: Up to 15 days, then it unlocks automatically

protocols.notes: Debit: only the reported card is cancelled. Credit: additional cardholder cards are cancelled too.

protocols.title: Payment sent but not received, or sent to the wrong account

steps.step: Work out which it is: the payee says it never arrived (trace) or it went to the wrong account (recall)
Draft a payment trace or a recall for the linked transaction
Submit the request; for a mistaken payment, the sending bank asks the receiving bank to return the funds
Tell the customer the rule that applies, based on how long ago the payment was made

required_checks: the transaction belongs to this customer and is outgoing
protocols.customer_message: We've started a {trace_or_recall} for your payment (case {case_id}). Recovery isn't guaranteed, and the timing depends on how long ago it was paid.

timeframes.rule: Request the return within 5 business days of the report (best practice: start within 2)
If funds are there and it's a genuine mistake, they are returned

timeframes.what: Reported between 10 business days and 7 months
timeframes.rule: Funds are frozen; the recipient has 10 business days to show they're entitled to them
Returned only if the recipient agrees

protocols.title: Customer in financial difficulty

steps.step: Respond with care; explain that hardship support exists and that a person will help
Draft notes: what changed, which products are affected, any vulnerability cues
Assess and agree any arrangement; refer to a financial counsellor where useful

officer_must: any arrangement or change to repayments
required_checks: extra care for customers in vulnerable circumstances (Banking Code of Practice)
protocols.customer_message: Thanks for telling us. A specialist will contact you about support options (case {case_id}).

protocols.title: Known merchant, wrong amount or service not received

steps.step: Suggest contacting the merchant first, checking receipts, and checking with any additional cardholders
If still pending, explain it can't be disputed until it finishes processing (usually up to 5 business days)
Draft the dispute with the transaction and evidence
Lodge the dispute; a dispute reference number is issued

required_checks: the transaction is no longer pending
protocols.customer_message: Your dispute is being lodged (case {case_id}). Disputes are usually resolved within 45 days of us receiving the information needed.

timeframes.rule: Usually resolved within 45 days of receiving the required information

protocols.title: Complaint about service

steps.step: Capture what happened, when, the outcome wanted, and any reference numbers
Acknowledge with a complaint reference number, review, respond, and explain the outcome and reasons

protocols.customer_message: Your complaint is recorded (reference {case_id}). We'll keep you updated and explain our decision.

protocols.title: Change of address, phone, email or other personal details

steps.step: Record the request; never make the change
Check for takeover signs: recent device or password change, new payees
Verify identity and make the change; name or date of birth changes need a branch visit with documents

officer_must: any change to personal or contact details
required_checks: one-time security code or officer identity check
protocols.customer_message: For your security, a person will make this change (case {case_id}).

protocols.title: When will my card arrive?

steps.step: Answer from card tracking: dispatch date, carrier, status, expected date
If past the expected date, prepare a replacement to the address on file
One-click approve the replacement (P4)

required_checks: address on file only; any address change goes to DETAILS_CHANGE
protocols.customer_message: Your card was sent on {dispatched} and is expected on {expected}.

protocols.title: General question about Westpac products or rules

steps.step: Answer only from the Westpac knowledge base, with the source link
If the knowledge base has no answer, say so and offer a person
